text: The organization is the IEEE Systems, Man, and Cybernetics Society (SMCS), part of IEEE. Its objectives are scientific, literary, and educational. It promotes professional standing, cooperation, technical-information exchange, meetings, technical-paper discussion, journals, and committee activity within its Field of Interest.
heading: SMCS Identity and Objectives

text: The SMCS Field of Interest includes integration of communication, control, cybernetics, stochastics, optimization, and system-structure theories; systems-engineering methods such as modelling, simulation, experimentation, human factors, design, testing and evaluation; and hardware/software applications to biological, ecological, socio-economic, social-service, computer-information and operational man-machine systems.
heading: SMCS Field of Interest

text: IEEE members of any grade, including students, may join SMCS if interested in its Field of Interest and after application and payment of Society fees. Qualified non-IEEE participants may become Society Affiliates under the criteria in the Society Bylaws and applicable fees.
heading: SMCS Membership

text: SMCS may collect annual assessments or fees in accordance with IEEE rules. It may charge registration fees for its meetings and may raise revenue through permitted means. Money held by or for SMCS legally belongs to IEEE and may be spent to promote SMCS objectives but not contrary to IEEE interests.
heading: SMCS Finances

text: SMCS is governed by a Board of Governors (BoG). All BoG members must be SMCS members. There are at most 27 voting members: two immediate Past Presidents, ten Administrative Officers, and fifteen Members-at-Large. Editors-in-Chief of fully sponsored SMCS Transactions serve without vote.
heading: Board of Governors Composition

text: A Member-at-Large of the BoG serves a three-year term, and at least five Members-at-Large are elected annually.
heading: Member-at-Large Term

text: SMCS officers include the President, President-Elect, Vice President for Organization and Planning, Vice President for Finance, three Technical Area Vice Presidents, Vice President for Publications, Vice President for Conferences and Meetings, and Vice President for Membership and Student Activities.
heading: SMCS Officers

text: The Executive Committee consists of the President, President-Elect, Vice Presidents, Secretary, and two immediate Past Presidents. The President chairs the ExCom. The Secretary and Treasurer are non-voting members of the ExCom.
heading: Executive Committee

text: The Secretary sends notices, prepares agendas, records BoG minutes, reports ExCom actions, keeps Society records, and makes required reports to the BoG, IEEE TAB, and under IEEE Bylaws.
heading: Secretary Responsibilities

text: The Treasurer reports through the Vice President for Finance and is responsible for sound financial practices, assisting with the Society budget, working with IEEE on financial matters, and processing expense reports.
heading: Treasurer Responsibilities

text: Each Vice President obtains subcommittee objectives in January and adds their own objectives. The Vice President for Organization and Planning prepares the Annual Plan and updates the Five-Year Plan annually for BoG approval.
heading: Annual and Five-Year Planning

text: A majority of voting BoG members constitutes a quorum. Proxy is not counted when determining quorum.
heading: BoG Quorum

text: When a quorum is present, a majority vote of voting members present is the act of the BoG unless otherwise provided. A person holding more than one position is limited to one vote. Proxy voting is not allowed.
heading: BoG Voting

text: SMCS may hold meetings, conferences, symposia or conventions alone or with other IEEE units or technical organizations, subject to IEEE rules. SMCS shall sponsor or cosponsor at least one major technical conference each year.
heading: SMCS Meetings and Conferences

text: SMCS periodically publishes its Transactions, Magazine, and eNewsletter as established by the BoG. Publication policies are governed by the Bylaws.
heading: SMCS Publications

text: Chapters may be formed under IEEE rules for purposes consistent with SMCS objectives. Committees are established by the BoG in special-interest areas within the SMCS Field of Interest.
heading: Chapters and Committees

text: An amendment to the SMCS Constitution may be initiated by a petition signed by five percent of SMCS members or by a two-thirds vote of the entire voting membership of the BoG.
heading: Constitution Amendment Initiation

text: SMCS Bylaws may be adopted or changed by a two-thirds BoG vote if proposed changes are sent to each BoG member at least two weeks before action. They require IEEE approval and publication before becoming effective.
heading: Bylaw Amendment

text: The Nominations Committee is chaired by the immediate Past President, subject to stated replacement arrangements. It includes the Chair and three Society members who, at selection, must have served on the BoG for at least one year.
heading: Nominations Committee

text: Vice President candidates must have been voting BoG members elected by the membership-at-large during the past five calendar years and served at least one full year by nomination. President and President-Elect candidates must have served at least one year as a Vice President.
heading: Candidate Eligibility

text: Additional Member-at-Large nominations require a written petition signed by at least two percent of SMCS members and filed with the Secretary at least 28 days before the election.
heading: Petition Nomination

text: The President and Vice Presidents serve two-calendar-year terms; the President-Elect serves one calendar year. Continuous service as President is limited to two years and continuous service as a Vice President in one office is limited to four years, subject to the stated partial-term rule.
heading: Officer Terms

text: The BoG meets at least once each year, usually around the Society Annual Meeting. The ExCom also meets at least once each year, usually about six months before the BoG meeting.
heading: BoG Annual Meeting

text: No BoG meeting may transact business unless each member has been notified of the time and place at least 20 days before the scheduled meeting.
heading: BoG Meeting Notice

text: The BoG or a committee may meet and vote using telecommunications that allow all participants to hear each other at the same time; normal voting requirements apply.
heading: Telecommunication Meetings

text: The BoG or a committee may take action without a meeting, such as by email vote. An affirmative vote of a majority of all voting members is required and the result must be confirmed and filed with the minutes.
heading: Action Without Meeting

text: The Vice President for Organization and Planning chairs the OPC. Responsibilities include annual Five-Year Plan updates, strategic and tactical planning, interpreting the Constitution and Bylaws when questions arise, and preparing modifications for BoG consideration.
heading: Organization and Planning Committee

text: The Systems Science and Engineering, Human Machine Systems, and Cybernetics committees provide leadership for technical activities such as conference special sessions, special publication issues, bibliographies, standards, technical meetings, workshops, and specialty committees.
heading: Technical Area Committees

text: The Vice President for Publications chairs the Publications Committee, which formulates, guides and evaluates SMCS publication policy and programs and supports the Transactions, Magazine, eNewsletter, website and related publication planning.
heading: Publications Committee

text: The Vice President for Conferences and Meetings chairs the CMC. The committee formulates, guides and evaluates SMCS conference and meeting policies and programs and coordinates Society technical meeting activities.
heading: Conferences and Meetings Committee

text: The Vice President for Membership and Student Activities chairs the MSAC, which coordinates membership and student activities, promotes chapters, maintains links between chapters and the BoG, supports speakers, and encourages student participation.
heading: Membership and Student Activities Committee

text: The Vice President for Finance chairs the Finance Committee and has overall responsibility for Society financial health, including budgets, financial monitoring, reports, investments and oversight of the Treasurer.
heading: Finance Committee

text: The Senior Past President chairs the Awards Committee, which nominates candidates for IEEE Awards, nominates recipients for SMCS awards subject to BoG approval, and maintains awards activities and policies.
heading: Awards Committee

text: The Fellow Evaluation Committee is chaired by the Senior Past President when eligible, or another appointed Fellow under the stated procedure. It evaluates IEEE Fellow candidates assigned to SMCS in accordance with IEEE evaluation procedures.
heading: Fellow Evaluation Committee

text: The SMCS President may appoint ad hoc committees. New committees and ad hoc projects may also be sponsored by at least three SMCS members who provide the proposed Field of Interest, organizers and initial members, and a first-year activity outline.
heading: Ad Hoc Committees

text: The Technical Area Vice Presidents are responsible for improving technical quality in their areas, chairing the corresponding area committees, encouraging and managing Technical Committees, collecting semi-annual reports, and handling recommendations or decisions on TC chairs, mergers, creation and dissolution.
heading: Technical Area VP Responsibilities

text: An Area Associate Vice President supports the corresponding Area VP, supports TCs, collects requests and opinions, analyses technical trends, assists planning for new, combined or discontinued TCs, promotes TC activities, and helps enforce policies and procedures.
heading: Area AVP Responsibilities

text: Technical Committees collectively define the scope of SMCS technical activities. Each TC must propose at least one special session at the annual SMC conference and should contribute through conferences, workshops, special issues, tutorial papers, newsletters and industry collaboration.
heading: Technical Committee Activity

text: All TC Chairs and Co-Chairs must be SMCS members. They must contribute to SMCS-sponsored conferences or workshops, recruit new members through TC activities, and report TC activities bi-annually to the corresponding Area VP.
heading: TC Chair Requirements

text: Yearly TC performance evaluation considers bi-annual reports and composition statistics, activities and publications, conference and event support, member acquisition, an up-to-date webpage, and future plans.
heading: TC Performance Evaluation

text: A request for a new TC is submitted to the corresponding Area VP with the TC name, Chair and member names, objectives and activity plan. The Area Committee checks the plan and overlap with existing TCs. After Area VP approval, activity may begin and the decision is reported and announced.
heading: Creating a New TC

text: A TC may be discontinued if inactive for at least one year with no credible revival plan, based largely on bi-annual reports. Alternatively, its Chair with support of at least two TC members may request discontinuation. The final decision rests with the corresponding Area Committee.
heading: Dissolving a TC

text: Major TC changes include changing TC Chairs or significantly changing technical content. The TC Chair proposes the change to the Area VP; after approval, the change is reported to the BoG, TCs are informed, and the change is announced.
heading: Major TC Changes

text: Annual Society dues for Members are set each year during the budget cycle. A change in dues requires approval by two-thirds of all voting members of the Board of Governors. Affiliate dues equal Society Member dues plus the IEEE-set Affiliate surcharge.
heading: SMCS Annual Dues

text: Society members are subject to IEEE and Society rules for material violations of governing documents, policies, the operational manual or the IEEE Code of Ethics, or conduct seriously prejudicial to IEEE. Discipline may include expulsion, suspension or censure by IEEE.
heading: Member Discipline

text: The Distinguished Lecturer Program is administered under the Vice President for Membership and Student Activities. Candidates submit specified biographical and lecture information, are evaluated by the committee, and normally receive two-year appointments with a possible two-year extension.
heading: Distinguished Lecturer Program

text: SMCS flagship conferences follow a rotating global schedule: Americas, then Asia/Oceania, then Europe/Africa, repeating on a three-year cycle. Hosting bids and proposals operate on a 24-36 month cycle.
heading: Flagship Conference Rotation

text: For financially sponsored or co-sponsored conferences, SMCS assumes full or shared financial responsibility. Revenue and expense sharing is defined in a Memorandum of Understanding, and conferences must comply with IEEE financial reporting and conference standards.
heading: Financially Sponsored Conferences

text: Technical co-sponsorship means direct and substantial SMCS involvement in the technical program without financial responsibility. SMCS may promote the event and encourage submissions and attendance.
heading: Technically Co-Sponsored Conferences

text: For flagship conferences, at least two bids should be obtained through a competitive process. The Conferences and Meetings Committee reviews proposals, the two strongest are recommended to the BoG, and the strongest proposal is approved following evaluation.
heading: Conference Proposal Review

text: A detailed conference budget should be developed early, covering venue, catering, marketing, travel, speakers and miscellaneous costs. The draft manual states a target surplus of 20 percent over projected expenses and calls for a contingency fund and approval by SMCS and IEEE.
heading: Conference Budget Planning

text: IEEE governance documents have a hierarchy. The Constitution contains fundamental objectives and organization; Bylaws implement constitutional provisions; Policies contain more detailed policies, objectives and procedures; organizational-unit manuals, policy statements and bylaws must conform to higher-level IEEE governing documents.
heading: IEEE Governance Hierarchy

text: An IEEE organizational unit is a subset of IEEE membership formed for educational, geographic, professional, technical or other appropriate activities. Each organizational unit is an integral part of IEEE rather than a separate organization.
heading: IEEE Organizational Units

text: Life Member designation applies when a member has reached age 65 and the sum of age and years of IEEE membership equals or exceeds 100. The designation becomes effective on 1 January of the following year.
heading: IEEE Life Member

text: Senior Member is the highest grade for which application may be made. A candidate requires professional maturity, at least ten years of professional practice, and significant performance over at least five of those years under the stated criteria.
heading: IEEE Senior Member

text: IEEE membership carries obligations to abide by the IEEE Constitution, Code of Ethics, Bylaws and Policies, support IEEE principles and activities, and meet applicable monetary obligations.
heading: IEEE Member Obligations

text: The IEEE Finance Committee reports to the Board of Directors and is responsible for financial strategy, financial issues, development of capital and operating budgets, and statements of allocated and unallocated reserves.
heading: IEEE Finance Committee
